And of this aptitude the man of imperfect self-control is destitute.
But there is no reason why the clever man should not be of imperfect self-control, and
the reason why some men are occasionally thought to be men of practical wisdom, and yet of
imperfect self-control, is this, that cleverness differs from practical wisdom in the way I
stated in a former book, and is very near it so far as the intellectual element is concerned,
but differs in respect of the moral choice.
